label: row_0
context: Alkyl amines show no chain-length effect from ethyl to propyl. Inductive withdrawal at the α-carbon depresses nucleophilicity: converting propylamine → glycine slows ~6.2×, while CF3 substitution (trifluoroethylamine) lowers rate by ~2.3×10^4 vs ethylamine. Aromatic heterocycles vary: aniline is ~8.7×10^4 slower than ethylamine, imidazole is moderately reactive (only ~27× slower than ethylamine), and pyridines are weak; electron-withdrawing substitution conjugated to the ring (nicotinamide) suppresses rate by ~70× relative to unsubstituted pyridine.
